value.reason: In models/card.ts:38-45, cardNum is a plain Sequelize DataTypes.INTEGER field. Its only constraints are isInt/min/max validators. There is no setter, hook or encryption/tokenization transform, so this matches the positive example and not the negative one, which uses encrypt() in a setter. data/datacreator.ts:271-277 writes Number(card.cardNum) directly through CardModel.create, and the finale-generated POST /api/Cards handler writes user-submitted card numbers the same way. Together these confirm that full card numbers are stored in plaintext in the SQLite database (models/index.ts:42, data/juiceshop.sqlite). The masking in routes/payment.ts:32,58 only affects API responses, not what is stored. The EFS volume holding the SQLite file has encrypted = var.efs_encrypted, so disk encryption depends on a variable whose value isn't shown. Even if it is enabled, it only protects the volume. It does not protect the field from anyone who can read the database through the app or a database connection. Financial card data is therefore stored without field-level encryption, masking or tokens, which is the safeguard Rule 6(1)(a) describes and the weakness CWE-311 names.
